analysis:
Reviewed both primary analyses and all replayed evidence independently. The changelog (changelog.d/coordinator-reconnect-stall.md:3-4), CLI reference (docs/provider/cli-reference.md head:443-447,1943), and telemetry documentation described in unit 1 consistently distinguish an absent registered session from coordinator acknowledgment; they do not establish runtime enforcement. No concrete security regression is supported by the supplied changes.
CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift head:53-100 extracts transport construction while retaining URL-based connection setup; head:136-148 replaces inline readiness handling with CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.start, a configured timeout, and centralized terminal-state mapping. This can improve availability, but its security-relevant guarantees now depend on implementations not replayed here. Against TB-002, TB-011 and T-053, verify exactly-once handshake completion, cancellation of timed-out transports, rejection of late callbacks, atomic installation of post-ready failure forwarding, and preservation of connection-specific authorization/nonce teardown.
The disconnected-drain contract also remains unresolved: inspect ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift and service drain callers to ensure unfinished terminal writes, response owners and native retirement are counted, and reconnect/registration cannot race admission fencing or acknowledgment decisions. Preserve confirmed process exit before logout/token deletion (A-008) and terminal billing settlement. These are changed integration contracts requiring further review, not findings inferred from missing source. Replay is incomplete (5 source units omitted); prior assertions about surrounding BASE code and telemetry lines could not all be independently verified. No supplied patch directly changes inference encryption, cache isolation (T-041), attestation policy, artifact qualification or privileged fan authority.
